Architecture frames the experience; nature lets it breathe. #Flexform #FlexformOutdoor #outdoor #collection #design #AntonioCitterio #madeinitaly #designlover

body:
“God is in the details” – Modernist Architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
This phrase could have been written about the Soft Dream sofa’s cast-metal feet. 
Their geometry lifts its silhouette, allowing it to hover just above the floor, introducing a subtle tension between solidity and suspension. Their sculpted proportions and exquisite finishes define the essence of the piece and are the silent signature of its design. #Flexform #TheEdit #SoftDream #sofa #design #AntonioCitterio #madeinitaly #interiordesign #designlover #living #indoor #collection

body:
At the heart of the Interior Landscapes project lies the concept that interior design is an integral part of a vast visual and emotional landscape, rich in subtle nuances. While it evokes the idea of an overarching display that embraces the diversity of shapes, solutions, and innovations that define Flexform’s design products, the title also carries an additional layer of meaning, encouraging visitors to explore the context in which the furnishings are placed. Each piece becomes part of a domestic landscape, blending seamlessly into spaces, emotions, and atmospheres.

“The Private Lives of Objects” unfolds within the geometric rhythm of the Chiostro Sant’Angelo, designed by Giovanni Muzio. Framed by aromatic Mediterranean plantings, the installation opens into a sequence of intimate settings where architecture, landscape, and design converge. Here, new pieces by Antonio Citterio, Monica Armani, and Sebastian Herkner reveal themselves – inviting a slower pace, a moment of pause, suspended between light, scent, and space.

With a signature sense of restraint, Patrick Norguet’s new pieces for Flexform feel both intentional and effortless. The Ozzy dining chair arrives on discreet casters – elegant, inviting, and designed to move with ease. The Louise collection plays with contrasts: smooth, enveloping cowhide set against the clarity of polished glass. Nightstands, etageres, and coffee tables that don’t demand attention, but hold it – defined by a light, unmistakable presence.
